(a) In General.—Subparagraph (N) of section 4132(a)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting “or any other vaccine against seasonal influenza” before the period. 
    (b) Effective Date.—
        (1) Sales, etc.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to sales and uses on or after the later of—
            (A) the first day of the first month which begins more than 4 weeks after the date of the enactment of this Act, or 
            (B) the date on which the Secretary of Health and Human Services lists any vaccine against seasonal influenza (other than any vaccine against seasonal influenza listed by the Secretary prior to the date of the enactment of this Act) for purposes of compensation for any vaccine-related injury or death through the Vaccine Injury Compensation Trust Fund.  
        (2) Deliveries.—For purposes of paragraph (1) and section 4131 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, in the case of sales on or before the effective date described in such paragraph for which delivery is made after such date, the delivery date shall be considered the sale date.

fable.w: The section amends the tax code's definition of taxable vaccines and sets an effective date tied to a listing action by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. The tempting reading is that the Secretary's listing implies rulemaking or public input, but the text neither requires nor authorizes a regulation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with any outside party. The only actor is a federal official, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: the date on which the Secretary of Health and Human Services lists any vaccine against seasonal influenza

qwen_block.w: This section defines the effective date of a tax amendment based on an administrative action by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. It does not require the Secretary to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or coordinate with non-federal entities before making that listing. The process described is purely internal to the federal government.
qwen_block.s: the date on which the Secretary of Health and Human Services lists any vaccine against seasonal influenza (other than any vaccine against seasonal influenza listed by the Secretary prior to the date of the enactment of this Act) for purposes of compensation for any vaccine-related injury or death through the Vaccine Injury Compensation Trust Fund.

opus.w: This section changes the tax code so that the vaccine excise tax covers any seasonal flu vaccine, and it sets the date that change takes effect. The tempting reading is that the HHS Secretary's listing of a vaccine is an agency decision that could involve outside input. But this section only uses that listing date as a trigger. It does not require or allow a comment period, rulemaking, consultation, a hearing, or a right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision here.
opus.s: the date on which the Secretary of Health and Human Services lists any vaccine against seasonal influenza (other than any vaccine against seasonal influenza listed by the Secretary prior to the date of the enactment of this Act) for purposes of compensation for any vaccine-related injury or death through the Vaccine Injury Compensation Trust Fund.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the effective date of a tax amendment based on an administrative action by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. It does not require the Secretary to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or coordinate with state/local governments before listing a vaccine. The listing is an internal federal administrative decision. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the date on which the Secretary of Health and Human Services lists any vaccine against seasonal influenza (other than any vaccine against seasonal influenza listed by the Secretary prior to the date of the enactment of this Act) for purposes of compensation for any vaccine-related injury or death through the Vaccine Injury Compensation Trust Fund.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary listing a vaccine for the Vaccine Injury Compensation Trust Fund involves consultation with outside experts or the public. However, the text itself does not mandate any such consultation; it merely sets a condition for the effective date of a tax amendment based on an administrative action by the Secretary. There is no requirement for public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with states/tribes before the Secretary makes this listing. The interaction described is purely internal to the federal government (Secretary of HHS making a determination) or involves the application of a tax law to sales.
